title: Collatz cycle infrastructure and small-cycle exclusions

problemStatement.formal: C(n)=\begin{cases}n/2,&2\mid n\\3n+1,&2\nmid n\end{cases};\ C(n)=n\Rightarrow n=0,\ C(C(n))=n\Rightarrow n=0, and the orbit of 1 has period 3.
problemStatement.plain: Backfill the Collatz-cycle metadata around the Lean results that are actually present: no fixed points except zero, no two-cycles except zero, the 1-4-2 cycle, contraction for `n % 4 = 1`, and small halving lower bounds.
whyMatters: The Collatz cycle question is an accessible dynamical-systems test case for arithmetic iteration.
Small-cycle exclusions and contraction lemmas are useful infrastructure even though they are far below Eliahou's large lower bound.
Correcting the old title avoids advertising the 17,087,915 lower bound as formalized here.

proven: `collatz_no_fixpoint` and `collatz_no_two_cycle` exclude fixed points and two-cycles except zero.
`three_quarter_contraction`, `min_cycle_length_j1` through `min_cycle_length_j4`, and `small_numbers_reach_one` provide basic cycle-constraint infrastructure.
open: Eliahou's 17,087,915 lower bound is not proved by the linked Lean files; `CollatzCycles.lean` and `CollatzCyclesOQ04.lean` record zero axioms and zero sorries for the smaller infrastructure.
knownResults.goal: Align the metadata with the verified Collatz-cycle infrastructure and mark the original Eliahou target as still open.
